# Reviewed exceptions for the "hardcoded credential literals" check in
# .github/workflows/ci-testing-pipeline.yml
#
# The scan greps src/ and api/ for any line carrying a KEY / TOKEN / SECRET / PASSWORD
# identifier together with a quoted 24+ character token — the exact shape of the five
# keys that were found hardcoded in this repo during the WS-1 security pass, including
# the `const X_API_KEY = process.env.X_API_KEY || 'literal'` fallback form.
#
# That shape also matches some legitimate non-secrets, mostly storage and cache key
# NAMES. Those go here, one exact match per line, with a comment explaining why the
# value is not sensitive. Anything the scan finds that is NOT listed here fails CI.
#
# Before adding a line, confirm the value is genuinely not a credential. If it is a
# credential: do not allowlist it. Move it to an env var read server-side in api/ via
# process.env, and rotate the exposed value (see docs/hardening/ROTATION.md).
#
# Lines must match the scanner's output exactly. To regenerate the current matches:
#
#   grep -rhoIE "(KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD)[A-Za-z_]*.*['\"][A-Za-z0-9_-]{24,}['\"]" src api | sort -u

# src/lib/ownpayEngine.ts — a browser localStorage key name, not a credential.
# It names the slot that merchant payout settings are saved under on the user's own
# device. Publishing it reveals nothing and grants no access.
KEY = 'astro360_ownpay_merchant_settings'
